A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-NLL research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original question-answering evaluations, rejection-accuracy results, and synthetic estimator experiments.

after.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices C–D report original simulations and question-answering evaluations, including the retained experiments and a new length-normalization comparison.

M1.justification: G-NLL remains the summed negative log-probability of tokens generated by greedy decoding: v1 Equation 11 matches v2 Equation 10. The new semantic-cluster formulation is left for future investigation and does not change the implemented G-NLL procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TriviaQA, SVAMP, and NQ-Open with short-phrase and full-sentence answers. Synthetic coverage also remains vocabulary sizes 20 and 100 and sequence lengths 2–4. Discussed summarization and OOD applications do not constitute new evaluations.

E2.justification: The main comparators remain PE, LN-PE, SE, LN-SE, and D-SE. V2 adds LN-G-NLL in Table 4 and adds beam-search and greedy-decoding comparisons to the entropy-estimation panels in Figures 1 and 4.

E3.justification: The synthetic evaluation is substantively revised: maximum-probability estimation becomes negative maximum log-probability estimation, the lower sampling temperature changes from 0.5 to 0.7, and v2 describes importance-weighted entropy estimation with weight clipping. The main question-answering models, sampling budget, correctness criteria, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a focused ablation testing whether length normalization helps G-NLL, and the existing synthetic estimator sensitivity analyses are revised. The TriviaQA decoding ablation in Figure 2 and the five-beam comparison already existed in v1.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix A explicitly omits standard errors; v2 Table 1 adds standard errors and significance markers against the best sampling-based comparator at p < 0.05. The reported appendix simulation count changes from 1,000 to 2,000 runs. V2 does not specify how the benchmark standard errors or significance tests were calculated.

E6.justification: All matched benchmark values in v1 Tables 1–4 are retained in v2 Tables 1, 5, 2, and 3. V2 adds aggregate rows and length-normalization results, including AUROC 0.532 for LN-G-NLL versus 0.649 for G-NLL on pretrained 8B long answers. Revised simulations report different low-temperature variance behavior under changed settings, although Figure 4's caption contradicts the revised text.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Theorem 1 and Appendix B's sample-complexity bounds and proofs for maximum log-likelihood and importance-weighted entropy estimation, with new boundedness and proposal-distribution assumptions. Appendix A.2 also adds a formal semantic-cluster uncertainty decomposition and defines MCP.

C1.justification: The central claims about principled single-sequence uncertainty estimation, greedy approximation, efficiency, and competitive performance remain. V2 additionally makes comparative estimation complexity an explicit contribution and claims that sampling-based or length-normalized alternatives can harm approximation quality, while more explicitly attributing MSP to earlier work.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations based on probability concentration, importance-weight variability, and length normalization diluting informative low-probability tokens. It expands the semantic-efficiency tradeoff and states the requirement for generated-token probabilities. It also qualifies v1 Appendix C's beam-search improvement claim, describing the retained results as showing no significant improvement over greedy decoding.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code/data access link, hardware information specifying eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs, approximately 100 node hours, and simulation weight-clipping details. Some existing details disappear: Figure 2 no longer identifies Llama-3.1-8B, and the rejection-table caption drops the explicit mapping of the two LLM judge variants.

R1.justification: V2 more explicitly positions its contribution as theoretically justifying existing MSP and distinguishing it from perplexity-based baselines. It adds discussion or citations for work including Vashurin et al., SPUQ, Graph Uncertainty, and Rényi entropy. The broader positioning relative to predictive and semantic entropy remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The synthetic study moves into a new theoretical-analysis section before the LLM experiments, and the appendices are reorganized around derivations, theory, simulations, and experimental details. The title changes, and ethics and reproducibility statements are restructured.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 4, and 5 are redrawn with revised quantities, axes, and comparison curves. Table 1 gains uncertainty annotations and an average row; a length-normalization table is added, and retained appendix tables are reordered and reformatted. The document also adopts ICLR headers and layout.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful length-normalization evidence, clearer attribution, and reproducibility and uncertainty reporting. However, its new entropy bound relies on Appendix B.2's invalid inference that c(y)log p(y) lies in [aC,bC] merely because c(y) ≤ C. Figure 4's caption also contradicts the revised simulation discussion. These problems affect the added theoretical support, leaving the net quality benefit unclear.
